doc.title: Bill Allred interviewed by Monk Rowe, Orlando, Florida, February 24, 2017

title: Name that trombone player: McPartland tour and Spider Ridgeway
summary: After an audio clip of Jimmy McPartland's band, he tells how a PE teacher kept drummer Spider Ridgeway sober on tour.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: I want to play name this trombone player.
Playing a lot of my licks.
Okay well that makes sense because that’s you.
Oh McPartland. Oh my God. And then I was so careful because I said you can’t do too much.
I like it. That comes from our library.
I’ve got a great story on this one. You’ve got time?

Herman Foretich, his nickname was “Dirty Shirt” it seemed like he never changed his shirt. But Spider Ridgeway was a good drummer. I mean he knew how to play trad. He could lay it on you and just make you play, you know, one of those drummers. And he was also a hopeless drunk. I mean he’d get started drinking and he’s gone for the weekend. So we were getting ready to go on this tour which — I don’t have this either , one of these days I’ve got to get it. But I think I’ve got a tape somewhere. Wow. Billy Allred.

Of Las Vegas. But anyway, so Jimmy had heard Spider play and he knew he wanted that sound. So he hired a guy from a local high school, a big barrel-chested PE teacher, and he assigned him to Spider Ridgeway. He said, “If he touches a drink kick his ass.” I mean this guy stayed with him. And Spider would tell us, “Oh man I’d love to have a drink but this bastard won’t —.” That’s the way he talked. And he had a spotless tour. Man he kicked that band all during the thing. We played and we ended up playing in Atlanta in the underground. And this guy kept him straight, and Jimmy paid him. Marian did a couple of tunes. God that was fun. Gene Mayl.
